sentences.text: Researchers conducted a retrospective analysis of patients with AL amyloid neuropathy treated at a university hospital in Paris, France.
Peripheral neuropathy was the initial sign in 77% of these individuals, while 43% presented with no other organ involvement, a condition the authors term pure neuropathic AL amyloidosis.
Within this specific subgroup, 80% exhibited a chronic, length-dependent axonal polyneuropathy, a pattern that is often nonspecific.
The IgM subtype accounted for 29% of the cases and was particularly associated with pure neuropathic AL amyloidosis.
For 20% of the patients, abnormalities in serum free light chains were the only hematological clue to the diagnosis.
